penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: A scanning/digitization service where quality matters requires human QA or at minimum human-guided mobile app usage per job; an automated Claude pipeline cannot correct physical book curvature from a distance.

rationale: The buyer is a vague mix of individuals, archivists, and small businesses — not a specific role with a budget line — and the pain is infrequent (a digitization project happens once, not weekly). The real technical challenge is computer vision and mobile-native image processing for page-curve correction, which is well outside Claude + simple-page tooling; existing apps (Adobe Scan, Microsoft Lens, Genius Scan) already partially address this, making differentiation hard. A solo non-technical operator cannot build a meaningful mobile app or reliable CV pipeline without significant engineering resources.
solution_plan: This is not a viable build for a solo non-technical operator using a Claude factory. The core feature (page-curve correction for bound books) requires mobile computer vision — not a Claude prompt + landing page. The closest viable pivot would be a 'document digitization concierge' service where customers mail documents and receive digitized files, but that introduces physical logistics and per-customer manual fulfillment, which the factory model explicitly penalizes. Do not pursue.
notes: Total 2.3 well below all thresholds. buildability_with_ai (3) and operational_autonomy (3) both fail build gates badly. requires_human_fulfillment penalty applied.
